core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Hajja corresponds to the Arabic form حجة (Arabic root ح ج ج (ḥ-j-j); حاجة / حاجّة (ḥājja)). Its core sense is pilgrim (one who performs the hajj). Hajja is the colloquial feminine of حاجّ — a woman who has performed the Hajj (also frequently written حاجة). The source gave the form حجة, which is really the noun 'a ḥujja (proof, argument)'; the intended sense is the pilgrim title.
